title: Twelve baskets left (John 6:1–15)
hookLine: gather the fragments so nothing is lost

cards: A crowd on a grassy hillside by the Sea of Galilee, about five thousand men, John says. Passover is near, the feast that remembers the night Israel left Egypt.

Jesus asks Philip, as a test: where shall we buy bread for all these? Philip does the math and gives up: "Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a little."
Not even a little each. Then Andrew notices a boy.

teach.h: A BOY WITH FIVE BARLEY LOAVES.
teach.b: Andrew says: "There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?"
Matthew, Mark and Luke tell this story too, but John is the one who mentions the boy, and that the loaves were barley. A kid's lunch, offered to a crowd. Jesus has everyone sit on the grass.
He takes the loaves, gives thanks, and hands them out, and the fish too, as much as anyone wants. Everyone eats until full.
The Gospels don't describe how it happened, only what people saw: enough.
Then the part this day is named for: "Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost." The disciples go around the hillside collecting broken pieces, and fill twelve baskets.

A miracle has just happened, and the next thing Jesus cares about is the crumbs. Twelve baskets: one for each disciple doing the gathering, maybe, or a number some readers connect with the twelve tribes of Israel.

All four Gospels tell this feeding, and some Christians hear in it the Lord's Supper too: he took bread, gave thanks, and gave it. And the scene ends strangely. The crowd wants to seize Jesus and make him king by force.

teach.h: HE SLIPS AWAY FROM A CROWN.
teach.b: He slips away alone, up the mountain.
He came to feed them, not to be crowned by them.

how: Some Christians give thanks before meals, as Jesus does here, and some churches run food banks and community meals, gathering surplus food so nothing is wasted.

o: crumbs swept away and thrown out afterward
the five loaves the boy gave before the meal
the broken pieces left over after everyone ate

games.q: five thousand people have just eaten their fill. you're a disciple. what does Jesus ask you to do next?
o: ask the boy for more food.
games.why: "gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost." they fill twelve baskets.

practice: Picture your kitchen, half a loaf, a few vegetables, last night's rice, and find one thing that might get thrown out that you could use.
Then widen it: a half-finished letter, an hour you usually waste, a small skill nobody asks for.
If you pray, give thanks for what's already there, the way Jesus gave thanks over a boy's lunch; if you don't, simply notice how much is there.

wordCard.voice: Fragments. What the disciples gathered after five thousand ate, so that nothing would be lost: twelve baskets of broken pieces.

orig.note: Greek: broken pieces, fragments. The word for what was left over.

carryVoice: Your line: let nothing be lost. Even the crumbs count, all twelve baskets of them. Rest well.
